sub: Web security: OWASP Top 10, SSL/TLS, CSRF, XSS and SQL injection prevention
def: Web security is the discipline of keeping untrusted input from being interpreted as code, keeping requests and identities from being forged, and keeping data confidential and authentic in transit, organised for study around the OWASP Top 10 categories and their concrete countermeasures.
exp:
The OWASP Top 10 is an awareness document listing the most consequential categories of web application risk, revised every few years from collected vulnerability data. In the 2025 revision the categories are broken access control, security misconfiguration, software supply chain failures, cryptographic failures, injection, insecure design, authentication failures, software or data integrity failures, security logging and alerting failures, and mishandling of exceptional conditions. It is worth knowing the 2021 revision alongside it, since older question papers and textbooks use it: there the order ran broken access control, cryptographic failures, injection, insecure design, security misconfiguration, vulnerable and outdated components, identification and authentication failures, software and data integrity failures, security logging and monitoring failures, and server-side request forgery. Two continuities survive every revision and are the safe things to assert. Broken access control has headed the list in both, and cross-site scripting is no longer its own entry because it was folded into injection, which is the correct way to think about it anyway: XSS and SQL injection are the same defect, untrusted data crossing into a place where it is interpreted as code, differing only in which interpreter is at the far end.

SQL injection follows from building a query by concatenating a string. The database receives one text blob and cannot tell which characters the developer wrote and which the user supplied, so a value containing SQL syntax becomes SQL. The reliable fix is a prepared statement with bound parameters: the query template is sent and parsed first, the values are transmitted separately, and the parser never sees them as syntax, so a value of any shape whatsoever is treated as a literal. In PHP that is PDO or mysqli with placeholders; in Python it is passing parameters to the cursor's execute method rather than formatting them into the string, and an ORM does the same underneath. Every alternative is weaker for a reason. Escaping functions such as addslashes are character-set dependent and have been bypassed; blacklists that strip quotes and semicolons miss numeric contexts, comment syntax and encoding tricks entirely; stored procedures help only if they do not themselves build dynamic SQL; and suppressing error display merely converts an error-based attack into a blind or time-based one without closing anything. The one place parameters cannot help is identifiers, since a table name, a column name or an ORDER BY direction cannot be bound, so those must be validated against a fixed allowlist. Supporting measures are a least-privileged database account that cannot drop tables or read other schemas, and generic error pages so the schema is not disclosed.

Cross-site scripting is the injection of attacker-controlled script into a page so it runs in the victim's origin, inheriting that origin's cookies, storage and permissions. There are three shapes: reflected, where the payload comes back in the response to a crafted link; stored, where it is persisted and served to every later viewer; and DOM-based, where the page's own JavaScript takes a value from the URL or storage and writes it into a dangerous sink without the server ever seeing it. The defence is contextual output encoding at the point of use, because the escaping required inside HTML text, inside an attribute value, inside a URL and inside a script block are four different things. Better still is to avoid the interpreting sink altogether: assigning to textContent creates a text node, so the string is never parsed as markup, whereas assigning to innerHTML parses it. Where rich text genuinely must be rendered, sanitise with an established allowlist-based library rather than a regular expression, because stripping script tags catches none of the event-handler attributes, javascript URLs or nested-construct tricks. A Content Security Policy is defence in depth: it restricts which script sources the browser will execute, with nonces or hashes for the inline script you do intend, so an injected payload has nowhere to run from. HttpOnly on the session cookie limits what a successful XSS can steal but does not prevent the script executing.

Cross-site request forgery is a different vulnerability with different defences and this is the pairing that catches people. In CSRF the attacker never reads anything; a page under the attacker's control causes the victim's browser to issue a state-changing request to your application, and because cookies are ambient credentials the browser attaches the session cookie automatically. The server sees a fully authenticated request that the user never intended. The condition that makes it possible is precisely that automatic attachment, not any ability to read the cookie or the response. The defences are a synchroniser token, an unpredictable value bound to the session that must be echoed back in the request body or a custom header and that an attacker's page cannot read cross-origin; the double-submit cookie variant; the SameSite cookie attribute, whose Lax setting stops the cookie being sent on cross-site form submissions and whose None setting requires Secure; and origin or referer checking, with re-authentication for the most sensitive operations. Note the asymmetry: output encoding stops XSS and does nothing for CSRF, while a CSRF token stops CSRF and does nothing for XSS, and worse, an XSS bug defeats CSRF protection entirely, because a script running in your origin can simply read the token and use it.

TLS secures the channel. The handshake negotiates a cipher suite, the server presents a certificate chain that the client validates to a trusted root, and an ephemeral key agreement derives session keys so that a later compromise of the server's private key does not decrypt recorded traffic, which is forward secrecy. Modern practice is to serve only current protocol versions with authenticated encryption suites, to automate certificate issuance and renewal through the ACME protocol, to publish CAA records restricting which authorities may issue for the domain, and to send HSTS so a browser that has seen the site refuses plaintext for it thereafter. Certificate validation is not just chain building; the hostname must match, the validity dates must hold, and revocation should be checked, commonly through a stapled response the server supplies. What TLS does not do is the part examiners test: it protects data in transit and authenticates the server, and it has no effect at all on injection, on cross-site scripting, on broken access control or on data at rest. A perfectly configured HTTPS site with a concatenated SQL query is fully exploitable over an encrypted channel.

The remaining categories are worth a line each because the conventional paper asks for them. Broken access control usually appears as an insecure direct object reference, where changing an identifier in a URL returns another user's record, and the fix is a server-side authorisation check on every object for every request rather than hiding the link in the interface. Security misconfiguration covers default credentials, directory listing, verbose stack traces, unnecessary services and over-permissive CORS. Supply chain risk is managed with lockfiles, pinned versions, automated dependency and image scanning and a software bill of materials. Server-side request forgery is contained by allowlisting outbound destinations. Response headers do real work: a Content Security Policy, nosniff to stop content-type guessing, frame-ancestors to prevent clickjacking, and a restrictive referrer policy. Authentication needs rate limiting, multi-factor authentication and modern password hashing. Logging must capture security-relevant events with alerting attached and must not capture passwords, tokens or personal data. For an Indian public-sector deployment there is also an incident-reporting dimension, since CERT-In is the national agency to which cyber security incidents are reported and which issues directions on logging and reporting timelines for organisations operating in India.

Exam shape: MCQ items on this leaf are almost always a defence-selection question, given the vulnerability pick the measure that actually closes it, and the distractors are the plausible-but-partial fixes above. In the conventional half this is one of the most reliably essay-shaped leaves in the whole paper, set as explain the OWASP Top 10 with examples and countermeasures, or as differentiate XSS from CSRF and describe the prevention of SQL injection. Marks are lost by writing generic advice; name the mechanism and say what it does and does not cover.
facts: Broken access control has headed the OWASP Top 10 in both the 2021 and the 2025 revisions; cross-site scripting is no longer a separate entry because it was folded into the injection category.
Prepared statements with bound parameters prevent SQL injection because the query is parsed before the values arrive, so a value can never be reinterpreted as SQL syntax.
Parameters cannot bind identifiers such as table names, column names or sort direction; those must be checked against a fixed allowlist instead.
XSS comes in reflected, stored and DOM-based forms, and the DOM-based form can occur entirely in client-side code without the payload ever reaching the server.
Assigning to textContent creates a text node and never parses markup, whereas assigning to innerHTML parses the string as HTML and is an XSS sink.
A Content Security Policy restricts which sources of script the browser will execute and is defence in depth against XSS, not a replacement for output encoding.
CSRF succeeds because browsers attach cookies to requests automatically; the attacker neither reads the cookie nor reads the response.
SameSite=Lax stops the session cookie being sent on cross-site form submissions, and SameSite=None is only accepted together with the Secure attribute.
Ephemeral key agreement in a TLS handshake gives forward secrecy, so recorded traffic stays unreadable even if the server's long-term private key is later compromised.
HSTS instructs a browser that has already visited the site to use HTTPS for that host, closing the plaintext first hop, but it performs no encryption itself.
Insecure direct object reference is broken access control, and the fix is a server-side authorisation check per object per request, not hiding the identifier in the interface.
CERT-In is the national agency to which cyber security incidents are reported in India and which issues directions on logging and incident reporting for organisations operating there.
traps: CSRF and XSS defences are not interchangeable. A CSRF token or SameSite cookie does nothing about injected script, output encoding and CSP do nothing about a forged authenticated request, and an XSS bug defeats CSRF protection outright because the injected script can read the token.

Escaping untrusted HTML at storage time is not a substitute for output encoding: it neutralises only the sink of the day, leaves already-stored rows untouched, corrupts the value for non-HTML consumers such as an email or a CSV export, and protects no sink added later. Encode at output, or use a non-parsing sink such as textContent.

addslashes, character stripping and disabling error display are not SQL injection defences. The first is character-set dependent and bypassable, the second misses numeric contexts and comment syntax, and the third only turns an error-based attack into a blind one.
HTTPS does not prevent SQL injection, XSS or broken access control. It protects the channel; an injected query executes exactly as well over TLS.
Removing script tags with a regular expression leaves event-handler attributes, javascript URLs and nested constructs intact; sanitisation must be allowlist-based and done by a maintained library.
mnem: CSRF writes without reading, XSS reads and runs. So CSRF is stopped by proving the request came from your page, and XSS by making sure the data never becomes code.

sub: Architecture and scale: MVC, microservices, SOLID, event-driven systems, caching and queues
def: This leaf covers how a web application is structured to change and to grow: MVC separating request handling, domain logic and presentation, SOLID governing where change is absorbed within a codebase, microservices and event-driven messaging distributing it across independently deployable units, and caching and queues absorbing load at the cost of staleness and asynchrony.
exp:
MVC exists to keep three kinds of change independent. The model holds domain state, the business rules that maintain its invariants, and its persistence; the view renders a representation for the client; the controller interprets the incoming request, decides which model operation it means, and selects what is rendered in response. The controller is deliberately thin. It does not hold business rules, which belong in the model, and it does not generate the markup or JSON, which is the view's work, so a controller that validates, computes, queries and formats has absorbed both neighbours and is the standard fat-controller smell. The payoff is testability and substitutability: the same model serves an HTML view and a JSON API view without change. Django names the same three parts model, template and view, so its view corresponds to the controller and its template to the view, which is a pure naming difference and a favourite trick question. The related patterns differ in how the view is bound: in MVP the presenter drives a passive view through an interface, and in MVVM the view binds declaratively to observable properties of a view model, which is the shape modern component frameworks approximate.

SOLID is five principles about where change is absorbed. Single responsibility says a class should have one reason to change, which is about actors and change drivers rather than about counting methods. Open-closed says a module should be open for extension and closed for modification, and the diagnostic is exactly a switch or if-chain over a type code that must be edited every time a new type appears: the payment class with a case per payment method violates it, and the repair is to make each payment type an implementation of a common interface so adding one adds a class and edits nothing. Liskov substitution says a subtype must be usable wherever the supertype is expected without breaking the caller's expectations, so an override may not strengthen preconditions, weaken postconditions or throw where the base contract promises success; the classic breach is a square subclassing a rectangle, where setting the width silently changes the height and a caller's assumption fails. Interface segregation says a client should not be forced to depend on methods it does not use, favouring several narrow role interfaces over one wide one. Dependency inversion says high-level policy should depend on abstractions rather than on low-level details, and both should depend on the abstraction. Keep three things apart there: dependency inversion is the principle, dependency injection is the technique of handing collaborators in from outside rather than constructing them internally, and an inversion-of-control container is merely a tool that automates the wiring. Dependency management sits alongside as the practical version of the same concern, with semantic versioning signalling breaking, additive and corrective changes in the major, minor and patch positions, a lockfile pinning the entire resolved transitive tree so a build is reproducible, and a virtual environment or per-project vendor directory keeping one application's tree out of another's.

Microservices decompose a system into independently deployable services aligned to business capabilities, each owning its own data store. Independent deployability is the defining property, not size: several services sharing one database are a distributed monolith, with all the operational cost of distribution and none of the independence, because a schema change still forces a coordinated release. The benefits are independent scaling and release cadence, fault isolation, team autonomy and freedom in technology choice. The costs are all consequences of the network. A transaction can no longer span services, so a business process that must span them becomes a saga of local transactions with compensating actions and accepts eventual consistency. Any call can fail, be slow, or succeed without the caller learning so, which requires explicit timeouts, retries with exponential backoff and jitter, circuit breakers that stop hammering a failing dependency, bulkheads that stop one slow dependency exhausting the whole thread or connection pool, and idempotent handlers so a retry is harmless. Debugging needs distributed tracing with a correlation identifier threaded through every hop. The honest architectural advice is to start with a well-modularised monolith and extract services where an independent scaling or release need is demonstrated, because a boundary drawn wrong is far more expensive to move once it is a network call.

Event-driven systems invert the direction of coupling: a producer emits a fact about something that happened and does not know or care who consumes it, so consumers can be added without touching the producer. Two messaging shapes are distinguished and routinely conflated. A work queue is point-to-point, where each message is delivered to exactly one of a pool of competing consumers, which is how load is distributed for jobs such as sending mail or generating a report. A publish-subscribe topic, especially the durable partitioned log form, retains messages and lets several independent consumer groups each read the whole stream at its own pace and replay it from an offset. Delivery guarantees are the examinable core: at-most-once may lose messages, at-least-once may duplicate them and is what almost every practical broker gives, and exactly-once is not a property of the transport but an end-to-end effect achieved by making consumers idempotent or deduplicating on a message key. Ordering is guaranteed only within a queue or a partition, never across the topic as a whole, so anything order-sensitive must be keyed onto one partition. Messages that repeatedly fail go to a dead-letter queue rather than blocking the stream, and the dual-write problem, where a service updates its database and then fails before publishing the event, is solved with a transactional outbox that writes the event into the same database transaction and relays it afterwards. Command Query Responsibility Segregation separates the write model from one or more read models kept up to date by these events, and event sourcing goes further by making the event log itself the system of record.

Caching trades staleness for latency and load, and it exists at every layer: the browser, a CDN edge, a reverse proxy, an application cache such as Redis or Memcached, and the database's own buffers. The common pattern is cache-aside, where the application looks in the cache, and on a miss reads the database and populates the entry; read-through and write-through push that logic into the cache layer, and write-behind acknowledges the write and persists asynchronously, which is faster and riskier. Entries leave by TTL expiry or by an eviction policy such as least-recently-used or least-frequently-used, and invalidation on write is the genuinely hard part. The arithmetic is easy and worth showing: with a 1 ms cache hit, a 50 ms miss and a 90 percent hit ratio, mean latency is 0.9 times 1 plus 0.1 times 50, which is 5.9 ms; lifting the hit ratio to 95 percent gives 0.95 plus 2.5, or 3.45 ms, so the last few percent of hit ratio carry most of the benefit. The failure mode to name is the cache stampede, also called the dogpile: a hot key expires, thousands of concurrent requests all miss simultaneously, and they all hit the database at once and overload it. The mitigations are to let a single request rebuild the entry under a lock while the others are served the stale value, to refresh proactively before expiry, and to jitter expiry times so keys populated together do not expire together. That last point generalises: any large set of entries given an identical TTL will synchronise its own stampede.

Exam shape: MCQ items here are principle-attribution questions, name the violated SOLID principle or the named failure mode, and one-step architecture judgements. The conventional half leans on this leaf heavily, with compare monolithic and microservices architecture for a government application, or explain caching strategies and their invalidation problems, being standing questions. Marks come from stating the trade-off with its cost, so pair every benefit you claim for microservices or caching with the consistency or operational price it charges.
facts: In web MVC the controller interprets the request, invokes model operations and chooses what to render; business rules belong to the model and output generation to the view.
Django's model-template-view naming maps onto MVC with the Django view acting as the controller and the template as the view.
A switch or if-chain over a type code that must be edited whenever a new type is added violates the Open/Closed Principle, and is repaired by polymorphic dispatch over a common interface.
Liskov substitution is broken when an override strengthens a precondition, weakens a postcondition, or throws where the base contract promises success.

Dependency inversion is the principle of depending on abstractions, dependency injection is the technique of supplying collaborators from outside, and an IoC container is only the tool that automates the wiring.

Semantic versioning signals breaking, backward-compatible additive and corrective changes in the major, minor and patch positions, and a lockfile pins the whole resolved transitive tree for reproducible builds.
The defining property of a microservice is independent deployability with its own data store; services sharing one database form a distributed monolith.
A business process spanning services becomes a saga of local transactions with compensating actions, accepting eventual consistency in place of a distributed transaction.

A work queue delivers each message to exactly one of a pool of competing consumers, while a durable publish-subscribe log lets several independent consumer groups each read the whole stream and replay it.
At-least-once delivery is the practical default, so consumers must be idempotent; exactly-once is achieved end to end by deduplication, not provided by the transport.
Message ordering is guaranteed only within a single queue or partition, so order-sensitive messages must be keyed to the same partition.
With a 1 ms hit, a 50 ms miss and a 90 percent hit ratio, mean read latency is 5.9 ms; at a 95 percent hit ratio it falls to 3.45 ms.
traps: A per-type switch is an Open/Closed violation, not a Single Responsibility violation. Single responsibility is about having one reason to change; open-closed is about extending behaviour without editing existing code, and the exam sets these two against each other.

The controller is not where business logic lives and not what renders the response; options describing it as holding business rules or generating the HTML describe the model and the view respectively.

A cache stampede is a concurrency failure at expiry, mitigated by single-flight rebuild under a lock, stale-while-revalidate and jittered TTLs; changing the eviction policy or signing entries addresses a different problem entirely.
Microservices are not defined by being small. Splitting a codebase while keeping one shared database buys none of the independence and all of the network cost.
A message queue and a publish-subscribe log are not interchangeable: a queue distributes work so only one consumer sees each message, while pub-sub fans the same message out to every subscriber.
mnem: SOLID: Single responsibility, Open-closed, Liskov substitution, Interface segregation, Dependency inversion. For messaging, remember that at-least-once is what you get, so idempotence is what you must write.

sub: AI-assisted web development, generative AI APIs, Model Context Protocol, analytics, ethics and law
def: This leaf covers the newest layer of web engineering: language models assisting development, hosted generative AI APIs integrated into applications, the Model Context Protocol as an open standard for connecting LLM applications to external tools and data, web analytics as measurement, and the privacy, ethical and legal obligations that govern all of it in India.
exp:
AI-assisted development means language models participating in the writing of the application, as editor completion, as a conversational assistant, and increasingly as an agent that edits files and runs commands. The productive framing for an examination answer is that the assistant shifts effort from typing to reviewing, and that accountability does not move with it. Generated code can invent an API that does not exist, can reproduce an insecure idiom such as a concatenated SQL query because that idiom is abundant in its training data, and can name a package that was never published, which is a supply-chain hazard when an attacker registers that name. The controls are the ordinary engineering ones applied more deliberately: review every change, keep tests and static analysis in the pipeline as the gate rather than the author's judgement, pin and scan dependencies, and never paste credentials, unpublished citizen data or personal records into a third-party assistant, because that is a disclosure to a processor the organisation may not have authorised.

Generative AI APIs are ordinary HTTPS APIs with unusual properties. A request carries a model identifier and a sequence of messages together with sampling parameters such as temperature and a cap on output tokens; the response is billed by tokens consumed and constrained by a context window, and it can be streamed incrementally over server-sent events so the interface renders as the answer is produced. Latency is high enough that a synchronous request-response page is often the wrong shape, so long generations belong on a queue with the result delivered asynchronously. Two integration features matter architecturally: structured or JSON output, which lets the response be parsed rather than scraped, and tool or function calling, where the model returns a request to invoke a function that your code executes and feeds back, which is what turns a text generator into something that can act. Grounding is done with retrieval-augmented generation, embedding your own corpus into vectors, retrieving the passages nearest the query and supplying them as context, which reduces fabrication and keeps the answer traceable to a source. Two security rules govern the whole area. First, the provider key must live behind a backend proxy that authenticates the user, enforces quota and logs usage, because a build-time environment variable in a frontend is inlined into the shipped bundle and is readable by any visitor who opens the file. Second, prompt injection is real: any untrusted text the model reads, a web page, a user comment, a retrieved document, can contain instructions, so model output must be treated as untrusted input, never rendered with innerHTML, never executed, and never allowed to trigger a privileged action without an explicit confirmation. That is the same trust-boundary discipline as output encoding for XSS, applied one layer up.

The Model Context Protocol is an open protocol that standardises how an LLM application connects to external tools and data, so that N applications and M integrations need N plus M pieces of work rather than N times M. Its participants are the host, which is the AI application, the client, of which the host creates one per connection, and the server, which is the program that provides context. A server exposes three primitives: tools, which are executable functions the application can invoke to perform actions; resources, which are data sources supplying contextual information such as file contents or database records; and prompts, which are reusable templates for structuring an interaction. Each primitive has listing methods so a client can discover what is available at run time rather than being compiled against a fixed set, and tools additionally have a call method. There is a client-side primitive too, elicitation, by which a server can ask the user for additional information or for confirmation of an action. The protocol is layered: a data layer that exchanges JSON-RPC 2.0 messages and handles version and capability discovery, and a transport layer offering standard input and output streams for a local server running as a child process, and a streamable HTTP transport for remote servers, which uses ordinary HTTP authentication and is where OAuth-based authorisation fits. Note carefully what a server is not: it does not hold model weights, does not run inference and does not fine-tune anything. The model stays in the host application; the server only offers capabilities to it. Security follows from that: an MCP server is a privileged integration point whose tool descriptions and returned content enter the model's context, so servers must be trusted, scoped to least privilege, and gated by user consent for consequential actions.

Web analytics measures how the application is actually used, and the vocabulary is examinable in its own right. A page view is one render, a session groups a visitor's activity within an inactivity window, and a user is an identifier persisted across sessions, so the three counts are never equal and quoting the wrong one misstates the result. Bounce rate and conversion funnels describe drop-off; UTM parameters attribute arrivals to campaigns; sampling appears once volumes are large and must be disclosed when quoting figures. Modern analytics is event-based rather than page-view-based, since a single-page application performs no document load on navigation and must report route changes explicitly. Implementation has a privacy dimension that has become a design decision: third-party cookies are increasingly blocked, so first-party measurement, server-side collection from request logs, or self-hosted and cookie-less analytics are the durable options. Performance measurement overlaps here, with the Core Web Vitals covering loading, responsiveness to input and visual stability, measured in the field rather than in the laboratory.

The ethical, privacy and legal layer is examined with an Indian frame. Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, the individual whose data is processed is the data principal, the entity that determines the purpose and means of processing is the data fiduciary, and anyone processing on its behalf is a data processor. The consent standard is the operative concept: processing personal data generally requires notice describing the purpose in clear language, and consent that is free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by a clear affirmative action, limited to the data necessary for the stated purpose, and as easy to withdraw as to give. Applied to a portal that wants to set a persistent third-party analytics identifier, that means the notice and the consent must come before the identifier is set, with a genuine means of refusal and withdrawal; a pre-ticked box, a bundled consent covering unrelated purposes, or a reject option buried behind extra clicks is a dark pattern and not free consent. Anonymising the data later does not retrospectively cure processing that had no lawful basis, and a fiduciary cannot contract its responsibility away by designating its vendor as the fiduciary, since the entity that decided the purpose remains answerable. The Act also carries obligations of purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, reasonable security safeguards, notification of personal data breaches, and erasure once the purpose is served, together with data principal rights of access, correction, erasure and grievance redress, heightened duties for fiduciaries designated as significant, and specific protection for children's data including verifiable parental consent and a bar on tracking and targeted advertising directed at children. Alongside it sit the information technology law's intermediary provisions, under which a platform's safe harbour from liability for third-party content is conditional on observing prescribed due diligence, and CERT-In, the national agency for reporting and coordinating responses to cyber security incidents, which also issues directions on log retention and reporting. For citizen-facing services, consent-based document sharing through DigiLocker is the standard alternative to collecting and storing scanned documents at all, and public websites additionally carry accessibility obligations under the guidelines for Indian government websites, which are built on WCAG.

Ethics goes beyond compliance and is where essay marks are actually won. Name algorithmic bias and its disparate impact on groups underrepresented in training data, the duty to disclose that a user is interacting with an AI system rather than a person, the requirement for meaningful human review before an automated decision affects an individual's entitlements, explainability of adverse decisions, the accessibility obligation as a matter of equity rather than of standards compliance, and the risk of over-collection simply because storage is cheap. facts: In the Model Context Protocol, an MCP server exposes tools, which are executable functions, resources, which are contextual data sources, and prompts, which are reusable interaction templates, to a client that discovers and invokes them.
The MCP host is the AI application and creates one client per server connection; the server holds no model weights and performs no inference.

MCP's data layer exchanges JSON-RPC 2.0 messages and handles version and capability discovery, while its transport layer offers standard input and output for local servers and a streamable HTTP transport for remote ones.
A frontend build-time environment variable is inlined into the shipped bundle, so a generative AI provider key must sit behind a backend proxy that authenticates users and enforces quota.

Prompt injection means untrusted text a model reads can act as instructions, so model output must be treated as untrusted input and never written to an HTML-parsing sink or used to trigger a privileged action unconfirmed.

Retrieval-augmented generation grounds answers by embedding a private corpus, retrieving the passages nearest the query and supplying them as context, which reduces fabrication and makes answers traceable.
In analytics, a page view is one render, a session groups activity within an inactivity window and a user is a persisted identifier, so the three counts differ and are not interchangeable.
A single-page application performs no document load on in-app navigation, so route changes must be reported to analytics as explicit events.
Under the DPDP Act 2023 the individual is the data principal, the entity determining purpose and means is the data fiduciary, and one processing on its behalf is the data processor.

The Act's consent standard requires free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous consent given by clear affirmative action, preceded by a plain-language notice of purpose, limited to necessary data, and as easy to withdraw as to give.
Children's data attracts verifiable parental consent and a bar on tracking and targeted advertising directed at children, and fiduciaries designated as significant carry heightened obligations.

Safe harbour for an intermediary under Indian information technology law is conditional on observing prescribed due diligence, and CERT-In is the national agency for cyber security incident reporting.
traps: An MCP server does not host or run the model. Distractors describing it as serving inference, fine-tuning on private documents or caching completions all misplace the model, which stays in the host application.

Consent must precede the setting of a tracking identifier. Anonymising or deleting the data after a retention period does not retrospectively supply a lawful basis, and naming the analytics vendor as the fiduciary does not transfer responsibility away from the entity that chose the purpose.

Moving a generative AI key from the frontend to a backend proxy is about exposure, not capability. Browsers can set an Authorization header and can read a streamed body, so options claiming those are impossible are wrong on mechanism.
Model output is not trusted content. Rendering a generated string with innerHTML or executing generated code without review reintroduces XSS and remote-code risk through a new door.

A pre-ticked consent box, bundled consent covering unrelated purposes, or a refusal option hidden behind extra clicks is a dark pattern rather than free consent, even though a consent banner is technically present.
